batchName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: After Zama, Scipio took the agnomen Africanus. What is an agnomen?
questions.explanation: Africanus means “the African”, for his victory over Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: He took the honorary surname (*agnomen*) Africanus, "the African".

questions.question: At Zama, who filled the open lanes between the Roman maniples?
questions.explanation: Most of Hannibal’s elephants ran down the lanes, where they were cut off and killed.
questions.sourceQuote: leaving open lanes filled with light skirmishers (*velites*).

questions.question: What was the triumphus Scipio celebrated in 201 BC?
options: The grand victory parade through Rome
questions.explanation: He also deposited about 40 tonnes of silver in the treasury.
questions.sourceQuote: Scipio returned home to celebrate a triumph (*triumphus*), the grand victory parade through Rome.

questions.question: In 213 BC Scipio was elected aedilis. What did an aedile do?
options: Looked after the city’s streets and festivals
questions.explanation: A tribune objected that Scipio was too young, but backed down before the crowd.
questions.sourceQuote: In 213 BC voters elected him aedile (*aedilis*), an official who looked after the city's streets and festivals.

questions.question: Who was the princeps senatus who fought Scipio’s plan to invade Africa?
options: The leader of the Senate, an elderly cautious general
questions.explanation: He may have been partly driven by jealousy of Scipio’s popularity.
questions.sourceQuote: The leader of the Senate (*princeps senatus*), an elderly general famous for his cautious strategy, fought Scipio's plan hard.

questions.question: How did Scipio change the usual layout of his manipuli at Zama?
options: He lined them up one behind another, leaving open lanes
He packed them into one deep block
He hid them behind the cavalry
He spread them out in a single long line
questions.explanation: Normally the maniples stood staggered like a chessboard.
questions.sourceQuote: Normally his infantry companies, the maniples (*manipuli*), stood staggered like a chessboard.

questions.question: In 210 BC Scipio received imperium pro consule. Why was that extraordinary?
options: He had never held one of Rome’s senior offices
He was not a Roman citizen
He had lost a battle in Spain
questions.explanation: He was the first Roman given such power without first serving as consul.
questions.sourceQuote: yet he received the full military authority of a consul (*imperium pro consule*).

questions.question: What was Scipio’s rank at Cannae in 216 BC?
options: Military tribune (tribunus militum), a junior officer
questions.explanation: He survived the disaster and rallied the stragglers.
questions.sourceQuote: In 216 BC Scipio served as a military tribune (*tribunus militum*), a junior officer, at Cannae
